basics.name: Hugo Silva
basics.label: Backend Software Engineer @ Datadog | Distributed systems, Go, Rust
basics.summary: Backend engineer with 7+ years building reliable, cost-efficient distributed systems. At Datadog, shipped JavaScript Debug IDs, cutting duplicated symbol ingestion by 95%+, delivered native crash symbolication across Windows, macOS, iOS and Linux, and cut on-call pages by 98%. Strong in Go, Rust/CGo, caching and cross-team ownership

work.name: Datadog
work.summary: Backend engineer on the RUM error deobfuscation platform (Go, Rust/CGo), focused on symbolication, caching, reliability and cost efficiency
highlights: Led end-to-end delivery of JavaScript Debug ID support across 10+ services (intake, API, UI), cutting duplicated symbol ingestion by 95%+ for the largest org
Shipped native crash (minidump) symbolication for Windows, macOS, iOS and Linux: CFI cache generation, Rust/CGo bindings and upstream fixes to the Symbolic library
Built a disk cache for symbol files (mmap, batched lookups, stream-to-disk, multi-key aliases), cutting S3 GET requests by 40%+; identified gp3 disk bottlenecks and drove rollout with partner teams
Implemented a per-frame distributed cache for JS unminification, stabilizing latency (p95 40ms → 4ms, p99 180ms → 120ms)
Cut sourcemap-processor on-call pages by 98% after reducing OOM kills by 99%
Automated Electron symbol ingestion with a scheduled upload job, stepping in to unblock the pipeline during limited team bandwidth
Enabled sourcemap uploads via a public API and authored its public documentation (JSON schema, Debug ID lookup)

work.name: Datadog
work.summary: Led reliability work on the RUM deobfuscation stack and resolved high-impact production issues across engineering teams
highlights: Eliminated 100+ weekly production crashes (→0) via root-cause analysis, deterministic memory fixes and an allocator migration in a high-throughput deobfuscation service
Drove splitting a critical service into independently scalable deployments and owned a cross-team Rust/CGo FFI library upgrade
Unblocked Next.js + Turbopack customers from source code integration failures, shipping the fix across multiple services
Introduced LLM-powered automation (-50% operational burden) and Terraform-managed dashboards, monitors and runbooks
